summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every sudo-invoked command (with user, timestamp, cwd, and command line) to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log, and disabled sudo's syslog output so these entries do not appear in the general system log (/var/log/secure or /var/log/messages). Verified the configuration survives a full node restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: RHEL 7.9, sudo 1.8.23, SELinux enforcing, rsyslog routes authpriv to /var/log/secure and excludes it from /var/log/messages
Created /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-command-logging with 'Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"' and 'Defaults !syslog', validated with visudo -cf, set mode 0440
Created /var/log/sudo-commands.log owned root:root, mode 600, restorecon-verified SELinux context var_log_t

Ran test sudo commands and confirmed entries (date, invoking user, TTY, PWD, target USER, COMMAND) were written to the new logfile and that no command-level sudo entries appeared in /var/log/secure or /var/log/messages afterward
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, sudoers drop-in content, logfile perms/context, and log line count
Restarted node1 via 'systemctl reboot' (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (fe422859... -> f09b29d0...) and uptime reset, proving an actual reboot occurred

Post-restart, verified sudoers config persisted, logfile perms/context intact, new sudo commands still logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user/timestamp, and /var/log/secure still excludes command-level detail

evidence.requirement: sudo commands recorded with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Created sudoers Defaults logfile drop-in, secured the logfile, then captured sudo command entries (timestamp, user, command) written to /var/log/sudo-commands.log

evidence.requirement: sudo command entries kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Added 'Defaults !syslog' to disable sudo's syslog output; confirmed /var/log/secure and /var/log/messages show only generic PAM session lines, no COMMAND= detail, after the change
Captured boot_id, sudoers config, logfile permissions/context, and log line count prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Triggered backgrounded systemctl reboot (ack returned before disconnect), observed connection timeout during reboot, then reconnected with a new boot_id (fe422859...->f09b29d0...) and fresh uptime, proving an actual restart

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of sudo command logging
evidence.summary: Confirmed sudoers drop-in, logfile ownership/permissions/SELinux context, and functioning sudo-commands.log logging (with user/timestamp) all persisted and worked correctly after reboot, while /var/log/secure remained free of command-level entries
